title: Financial Forensics
standfirst: Detecting fraud and financial misconduct through data — from Benford's law to modern anomaly detection.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the fundamentals of finance and accounting, including the lifecycle of financial transactions and applications of AI/ML in the finance industry. It also covers model explainability in regulated environments and explores real-world problems such as credit card fraud, identity fraud, and anti-money laundering.
faculty: Prof. G Arun Kumar, Department of Management Studies, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Introduction to finance and accounting; Fundamentals of financial accounting.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Financial statements; Balance sheet and income statement analysis.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Cash flow statement; Cash flow analysis and interpretation.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Integrated analysis of financial statements; Linking financial reports.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Financial ratios; Performance evaluation and analysis.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Corporate finance basics; Time value of money; Financial decision-making.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Advanced corporate finance concepts; Investment and financing decisions.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Transaction lifecycle; Credit risk fundamentals; Probability of default modeling; Credit risk optimization.

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: Financial fraud detection; Supervised and unsupervised learning approaches; Practical fraud analytics.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Time series analysis; Components and forecasting models; Hands-on modeling.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: Text analytics for financial forensics; Text preprocessing; Entity resolution.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: Explainable AI (XAI); SHAP-based interpretability; AI/ML applications in financial forensics.
